parsed_answer.content: In systems programming and technical interviews, manipulating contiguous memory segments efficiently is a baseline requirement. Arrays and Strings serve as the foundational data structures for evaluating algorithmic competence in Java. When dealing with large linear collections, naive nested iteration leads to $O(N^2)$ quadratic time complexity, which fails instantly under production loads. To optimize these workloads, modern software engineers rely on three algorithmic patterns: two pointers, sliding window, and prefix sums. The two-pointers technique involves maintaining two index references—often moving inward from opposite ends or tracking relative paces—to process linear data in a single pass of $O(N)$ time. The sliding window pattern dynamically expands or shrinks a window bound by left and right indices, transforming subarray problems into manageable $O(N)$ operations by avoiding redundant recalculations. Finally, prefix sums precompute cumulative totals of an array to answer arbitrary range-sum queries in $O(1)$ constant time after an initial $O(N)$ preprocessing phase.

items: Two Pointers leverage sorted properties or structural symmetry, allowing left and right indices to converge conditionally without extra memory allocations.
Sliding Window maintains an invariant state (such as character frequencies or current sums) within a dynamic boundary, updating edge elements as the window shifts right.
Prefix Sum arrays store running totals where the sum of elements from index i to j is efficiently calculated as P[j+1] - P[i], eliminating inner loops.

parsed_answer.content: Beware of off-by-one errors when implementing prefix sums and sliding windows. In prefix sum arrays, always size your auxiliary array to `nums.length + 1` to handle zero-indexed range boundaries cleanly without complex conditional branching. When handling Java Strings inside sliding windows, remember that `String.charAt()` on standard UTF-16 strings can hide performance pitfalls if you deal with surrogate pairs; consider operating on `char[]` arrays directly for high-throughput stream processing.
